     Spotted Eagle       Found in reef areas and sandy bottoms.        6
                         The spotted eagle ray has a poisonous
                         spine on its tail and incredibly
                         powerful jaws to crush oysters, clams,
                       and numerous crustaceans.  Divers report
                          large schools during breeding season.
                                                               
                          This ray is an active swimmer and often
                                            leaps into the air.  The slapping sound
                       it makes on the water is thought to mark
                                                   a territory.
                                                               
                                             Edibility is poor.
                                                               
                               Range is throughout the tropics. bottom
    Total length 256.0
    Scorpionfish
     Firefish                     Also known as the turkeyfish.  Inhabi7s7
     Pterois volita                    reef caves and crevices.  The firefish
                          is usually stationary during the day,
                                   but feeds actively at night.  Favorite
                                         foods are crustaceans.
                                                               
                                         The dorsal spines of the firefish are
                       needle-like and contain venom.  They can
                            inflict an extremely painful wound.
                                                               
                                             Edibility is poor.
                                                               
                                             Range is from Western Australia to
                                                      Malaysia.
                                                                bottom
    Total length 38.0

    Sculpin
     Cabezon            Often called the great marbled sculpin.        8
                                     Found over rocky or shell-encrusted
                                     bottoms from shallow to moderately deep
                                                        waters.  It feeds primarily
                                      crustaceans and mollusks.
                                                               
                                      The male cabezon will not budge while
                                      guarding its nest and can even be
                                             touched by divers.
                                                               
                        Edibility is good; the flesh is bluish-
                             green but turns white when cooked.  The
                             eggs of the cabezon are poisonous.
                                                               
                          Range is from Alaska to Central Baja. bottom
    Total length 99.0

     Nurse Shark                                               F157.48t10 found und157.4810
                       ledges.  Carnivorous with well-developed
